Marquette Greene-Scott

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 22, Harris County, Texas · Open seat

Attorney; Mayor Pro Tem, City of Iowa Colony, Texas

Marquette Greene-Scott is a civil attorney, a former math teacher, and mayor pro tem of Iowa Colony, Texas, in Brazoria County. She was the Democratic nominee for Texas' 22nd Congressional District in 2024 and lost the general election to Rep. Troy Nehls. On March 3, 2026, she won a five-candidate Democratic primary with 54.6% of the vote and faces Republican Trever Nehls in the November 3, 2026 general election for the open seat.

Where Greene-Scott stands

Bipartisanship / approach to Congress
Says Congress is broken and bipartisanship has become taboo. Pledges to research each issue and vote for what is best for the district rather than along party lines, pointing to her city council record.
Immigration
Supports working on a broad deal in Congress that would include a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers.
Campaign priorities
Lists her priorities as creating jobs, improving infrastructure, and protecting essential rights. Other campaign issues: military families, borders and immigration, affordability, the economy, healthcare, voting rights, and reproductive rights.
Voting rights
Has held town halls on voting rights across the district as part of her 2026 campaign.

Background

  • Iowa Colony City Council, Position 3, 2021–present; currently mayor pro tem
  • Democratic nominee, U.S. House Texas District 22, 2024 (lost to Troy Nehls)
  • Won the Democratic primary for U.S. House Texas District 22 on March 3, 2026 (54.6%)
  • Attorney for about 21 years, focused on helping families and individuals through personal crises
  • Taught high school and college mathematics for 14 years; former Mathematics Department Chair, East Baton Rouge Parish School System
